questions.q: Why isn't a correctly written and reviewed control (from Lesson 25) automatically safe to enforce?
options: Report-only and audit modes don't exist for any real security tool
Reviewed code is always guaranteed to behave correctly in production
Being written correctly doesn't reveal what happens when real users, sign-ins, and devices actually hit the control
Testing is never necessary once a pull request has been approved
questions.explain: A policy that looks correct in a diff can still lock out a legitimate workflow — testing is how you find that out before enforcement.

questions.q: What does Conditional Access's report-only state actually do?
options: Evaluates every sign-in as if the policy were enforced and logs the outcome, without actually blocking or challenging anyone
Immediately blocks every sign-in that would fail the policy
Disables the policy completely with no logging at all
Only works for policies that require MFA
questions.explain: Report-only logs what the policy would have done so you can review real sign-in outcomes before flipping it to On.

questions.q: What are the four real states an Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rule can be set to?
options: On, Off, Pending, and Archived
Low, Medium, High, and Critical
Draft, Review, Approved, and Deployed
Not configured, Block, Audit, and Warn
questions.explain: Audit logs what would have been blocked without blocking it, Warn lets the user proceed past a warning, and Block stops the action outright.

questions.q: After a clean audit-mode or report-only run, what's the recommended next step before an org-wide rollout?
options: Scope the control to a small, representative pilot group first
Immediately enforce the control for every user in the organization
Wait indefinitely with no further action
Delete the audit-mode logs and skip straight to Block or On
questions.explain: A pilot group keeps the blast radius small if something was missed, instead of affecting every employee at once.

questions.q: What does "simulate first, enforce second" mean in the context of this lesson?
options: Always enforce a control immediately and simulate its effects afterward
Simulation replaces the need for peer review entirely
Validate a control's real-world effect (via audit/report-only mode and a pilot group) before turning on full enforcement
Only cloud-based controls can be simulated; on-prem controls cannot
questions.explain: Testing in a non-blocking mode and then on a pilot group, before full enforcement, is the pattern this lesson teaches.
